result.summary: This is a narrow residential street with sidewalks on both sides but a complete lack of pedestrian crossing infrastructure at the visible intersection. The presence of parked cars right up to the corner creates significant sightline obstructions for anyone attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to designate a safe crossing area for pedestrians at the intersection.

hazards.name: Missing curb ramps
hazards.description: The lack of curb ramps makes the crossing inaccessible for people with mobility aids, strollers, or carts.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk in the foreground

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corner block the view between drivers and pedestrians entering the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street near the corner

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile, sloped curb ramps at the corners to ensure universal accessibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with mixed-use land use, featuring sidewalks and a marked crosswalk across a side street. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the environment lacks modern safety enhancements like high-visibility markings, traffic signals, or physical buffers between pedestrians and vehicles.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings across the side street are significantly faded, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, crossing the side street next to the variety store.

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb near the intersection can block the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, where a line of cars is parked up to the intersection.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility continental or ladder markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sight lines for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and a marked zebra crosswalk, though the markings are significantly faded. While a stop sign controls the side street, the lack of high-visibility signage or signals at a crossing adjacent to a public park area presents a safety gap.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signage
